_comment: Authored analysis: ownership, lifecycle, refcount and locking judgements that no composer can derive, keyed to the C entities they describe. The structural half of each record (field layout, signatures, footprints, casts) is composed from the CodeQL tables on demand and merged in at read time, so a re-extract rewrites nothing here. Written only by `crustify-oracle <target> query {types,symbols} --update`; read through crustify.manifests. Hand-edit at your own risk: `--update` validates a submission against the composed skeleton (unknown field, wrong kind, ptr-invariant violation) and this file does not.

types.name: ACCESS_DESCRIPTION_st
types._comment_agent: ACCESS_DESCRIPTION is an ASN.1 SEQUENCE. Its generated destructor recursively releases both child pointers; public construction paths replace method and mutate location, and the published layout permits either slot to be cleared.

ptr.note: ACCESS_DESCRIPTION_new allocates the GENERAL_NAME child; construction code mutates it in place, and ACCESS_DESCRIPTION_free recursively releases any non-null installed child.
The sequence owns one ASN1_OBJECT_free obligation. The slot can contain a dynamic object or a static OBJ_nid2obj result (whose free is a no-op), and public field access can clear it.

types.name: ASN1_ITEM_st
types._comment_agent: ASN1_ITEM instances and every pointer they publish are immutable function-local static descriptors generated by asn1t.h macros; no lifecycle routine owns or releases the descriptor storage.

ptr.note: Optional process-lifetime descriptor selected by itype; it aliases a static ASN1_PRIMITIVE_FUNCS, ASN1_EXTERN_FUNCS, or ASN1_AUX value and is never freed through ASN1_ITEM.
All public ASN1_ITEM definition macros store a process-lifetime string literal; consumers use it directly as a non-null C string.
Process-lifetime static const template storage: null for types without templates, a singleton for ASN1_ITEM_TEMPLATE, or an array of tcount elements for SEQUENCE/CHOICE.

types.name: ASN1_TEMPLATE_st
types._comment_agent: ASN1_TEMPLATE values are generated as static const descriptors by the public asn1t.h macros. They own neither their item callback nor their field-name string. The item slot is a two-way discriminated union resolved through one function-pointer type: flags & ASN1_TFLG_ADB_MASK selects the ASN1_ADB reading, and is zero for an ordinary ASN1_ITEM.

ptr.note: ASN1_EX_TYPE and ASN1_EX_TEMPLATE_TYPE initialize this const char pointer with a stringized identifier, yielding a non-null immutable static NUL-terminated string.

ASN1_EX_TYPE and ASN1_EX_TEMPLATE_TYPE initialize this slot with ASN1_ITEM_ref(type) = type##_it; ASN1_ADB_OBJECT and ASN1_ADB_INTEGER initialize it with tblname##_adb. Both expand to a nullary function returning the address of static const storage, so the callable is non-null, immutable and process-lifetime borrowed. Its RESULT is discriminated, not the slot: flags & ASN1_TFLG_ADB_MASK nonzero means the returned pointer is an ASN1_ADB table rather than an ASN1_ITEM, which is exactly the test ossl_asn1_do_adb (crypto/asn1/tasn_utl.c:236), asn1_template_new (crypto/asn1/tasn_new.c:222) and asn1_item_embed_d2i (crypto/asn1/tasn_dec.c:402) apply before reading it.

types.name: NOTICEREF_st
types._comment_agent: ASN1_SEQUENCE(NOTICEREF) declares an owned DISPLAYTEXT and owned SEQUENCE OF ASN1_INTEGER. The generated constructor initializes both; notice_section mutates them; the generated full destructor recursively releases both fields.

types.name: POLICYINFO_st
types._comment_agent: ASN1_SEQUENCE(POLICYINFO) declares an owned ASN1_OBJECT and optional owned SEQUENCE OF POLICYQUALINFO. policy_section/r2i_certpol construct them; POLICYINFO_free recursively releases them; ossl_policy_data_new transfers both by nulling the source fields.

ptr.note: POLICYINFO owns the ASN1_OBJECT_free obligation. POLICYINFO_new installs the static NID_undef object, while public field access and transfer paths can clear the slot; users read or transfer the pointer but do not mutate the pointee.

Optional STACK_OF(POLICYQUALINFO): POLICYINFO owns the stack and each element; POLICYINFO_free pop-frees it, builders push owned mutable elements, and ossl_policy_data_new can transfer the whole field by clearing it.

types.name: POLICYQUALINFO_st
types._comment_agent: The pqualid OID is the ASN.1 ADB discriminator for the three one-pointer union arms and has runtime owned-versus-static-borrowed storage. Safe mutation must replace selector and arm together.

ptr.note: Owned ASN1_IA5STRING arm selected by NID_id_qt_cps and recursively released by the POLICYQUALINFO ASN.1 destructor.
Default ASN.1 ADB arm, active for selector OIDs other than id-qt-cps and id-qt-unotice; recursively released as ASN1_TYPE.
Owned USERNOTICE arm selected by NID_id_qt_unotice and recursively released by the POLICYQUALINFO ASN.1 destructor.

Runtime-conditional selector ownership: ASN.1 decoding and dynamic construction install owned ASN1_OBJECT values, while OBJ_nid2obj installs borrowed process-static registry objects. POLICYQUALINFO_free applies ASN1_OBJECT_free, which frees the dynamic case and intentionally leaves the static case allocated.

types.name: USERNOTICE_st
types._comment_agent: The ASN.1 sequence declaration marks both pointer fields optional and USERNOTICE_free delegates to ASN1_item_free, which recursively owns and releases both children.

ptr.note: ASN1_OPT(USERNOTICE, exptext, DISPLAYTEXT) makes this an optional uniquely owned ASN1_STRING; USERNOTICE_free releases it and notice_section writes its contents.

types.name: X509_algor_st
types._comment_agent: X509_ALGOR owns both pointer fields through its ASN.1 SEQUENCE template. X509_ALGOR_set0 transfers the algorithm object and parameter payload on success; sequence teardown releases algorithm with ASN1_OBJECT_free and the optional parameter with ASN1_TYPE_free. Direct code writes through parameter, while algorithm objects are treated as immutable after installation. Both slots can be null.

ptr.note: Owned AlgorithmIdentifier OID slot. X509_ALGOR_set0 frees the old object and transfers aobj on success; ASN.1 sequence teardown calls ASN1_OBJECT_free. Built-in objects are accepted because that destructor is intentionally a no-op for non-dynamic objects. Callers read but do not mutate the installed ASN1_OBJECT pointee.
Optional owned ASN1_TYPE. X509_ALGOR_set0 allocates, replaces, or frees it according to ptype, and sequence teardown releases it; multiple users update its discriminator and active payload in place.

types.name: X509_extension_st
types._comment_agent: The mandatory object pointer is an owned ASN.1 child. The ASN.1 sequence template initializes and frees it, and X509_EXTENSION_set_object replaces it after OBJ_dup while X509_EXTENSION_get_object only lends it.

ptr.note: Mandatory ASN1_SIMPLE child owned by the extension; full destruction releases its free obligation and set_object replaces the slot with an OBJ_dup result. The pointee remains shared because built-in objects may be static.

types.name: X509_name_entry_st
types._comment_agent: Both pointer fields are mandatory owned children of a fully initialized X509_NAME_ENTRY, as established by its ASN1_SEQUENCE template and public setter/free implementations.

ptr.note: Mandatory ASN1_SIMPLE field initialized by X509_NAME_ENTRY_new; the entry owns it, X509_NAME_ENTRY_free releases it, and set_object replaces it with an OBJ_dup result.
Mandatory ASN1_SIMPLE field initialized by X509_NAME_ENTRY_new; the entry owns and mutates the ASN1_STRING and X509_NAME_ENTRY_free releases it.

types.name: X509_name_st
types._comment_agent: The private layout is opaque on the public wrap surface. Its three pointer fields are nevertheless fully lifecycle-analyzed from x509_name_ex_new/free/canon/d2i.

ptr.note: x509_name_ex_new allocates the BUF_MEM and requires success; x509_name_ex_free releases it with BUF_MEM_free. Encoding grows and writes through it.
Owned canonical-encoding byte buffer of canon_enclen bytes. Empty names deliberately use NULL/zero; x509_name_canon replaces it and x509_name_ex_free releases it with OPENSSL_free.
Owned STACK_OF(X509_NAME_ENTRY), allocated during successful construction and mutated by name operations. Full teardown pop-frees its owned entries.

types.name: X509_pubkey_st
types._comment_agent: The public X509_PUBKEY surface is opaque. A complete object uniquely owns algor, public_key and propq, owns one EVP_PKEY reference when the optional decode cache exists, and only borrows its optional OSSL_LIB_CTX.

ptr.note: Unique X509_ALGOR child allocated/populated during construction, mutated by set0 operations, duplicated deeply, and released by X509_ALGOR_free. It is transiently null in zeroed/partially constructed storage but non-null for a fully formed public object.

Optional non-owning library context retained by new_ex/set0_libctx and passed into later decoder construction; no up-ref or free is performed, so the external context must remain live while the pubkey may use it.

Optional cached EVP_PKEY. The pubkey owns one reference: decode creates it and X509_PUBKEY_set takes an up-ref before storing it; x509_pubkey_ex_free pays that debt with EVP_PKEY_free. X509_PUBKEY_get0 exposes a mutable borrowed handle.
Optional NUL-terminated property query deep-copied with OPENSSL_strdup and released with OPENSSL_free; consumers only read it as a string.

Unique ASN1_BIT_STRING child allocated/populated during construction, mutated by public-key setters and decoding, duplicated deeply, and released by ASN1_BIT_STRING_free. It is transiently null only in partial construction.

types.name: _IO_FILE
types._comment_agent: Reviewed as an imported, permanently C-owned type. Its footprint is opaque everywhere: opaque_in is complete for the tree, and the only field touchers are glibc's own inline helpers in bits/stdio.h (getc_unlocked, putc_unlocked, feof_unlocked, ferror_unlocked), none of which this codebase calls. No OpenSSL, apps, ssl or test code reads or writes a single member, so the wrapper keeps the layout opaque and exposes no field accessors; the field judgements below record glibc's documented internal contract so that a later wave cannot mistake an interior pointer for owned storage. Stream lifecycle stays in libc: fopen/fdopen allocate and fclose releases. libcrypto never frees a stream it did not open (BIO_new_file opens and closes its own; BIO_new_fp and BIO_set_fp free the caller's stream only when the caller passes BIO_CLOSE), so the type has borrowed handles and no owning pointer form until an fclose-backed release strategy is scheduled.

ptr.note: First valid character of the backup area; an interior pointer into the _IO_save_base allocation, null when no backup area exists.

Start of the reserve area, with runtime-conditional ownership: normally a glibc-allocated buffer released when the stream is closed or re-buffered, but setvbuf can install caller storage and an unbuffered stream points at the inline _shortbuf member instead. The flag deciding which case applies is glibc-internal, so no wrapper may free this slot; null until the stream is buffered.
End of the reserve area started by _IO_buf_base; a bound rather than storage of its own, null while the stream has no buffer.
Start of the putback+get area inside the reserve area; interior pointer, null before a buffer exists, never released on its own.
End of the get area inside the reserve area; interior pointer maintained by glibc on every refill, null before a buffer exists, and never released on its own.

Current read position inside the reserve area delimited by _IO_buf_base/_IO_buf_end; glibc advances it and refills through it, and it is null while the stream has no buffer. It is an interior pointer, never separately allocated or released.

Start of the saved (non-current) get area allocated by glibc when the stream switches to its backup area; released by glibc when the backup area is discarded or the stream is closed. Null whenever no backup area exists, which is the state for every stream this tree opens.
End of the saved get area; a bound on the _IO_save_base allocation, null when no backup area exists.
Start of the put area inside the reserve area; glibc writes bytes through it when flushing, and it is null before a buffer exists.
End of the put area inside the reserve area; compared against _IO_write_ptr to decide when to overflow. Interior pointer, null before a buffer exists.
Current put position inside the reserve area; the __putc_unlocked_body macro stores through it and advances it. Interior pointer, null before a buffer exists.
Link into glibc's global list of open streams. Each linked stream is owned by whoever opened it, so following the chain must never transfer ownership; null at the end of the list.

Conversion state used once a stream acquires wide orientation; glibc attaches storage that lives with the stream's own allocation and mutates it while converting. Not separately released, and null for byte-oriented streams, which is every stream this tree opens.

Type-erased buffer the stream registers for release during glibc's process-teardown pass rather than at fclose. Ownership sits with the stream implementation; no code in this tree reads, writes or frees it, and it is null for ordinary streams.
Link into glibc's process-teardown (__libc_freeres) chain of streams. The linked stream belongs to whoever opened it, so this is a borrow; null outside that teardown bookkeeping.

Opaque _IO_lock_t (a void typedef outside libc) guarding the stream. glibc allocates it together with the stream, or points at static storage for the standard streams, and releases it with the stream; it is written by every locked stdio operation and is never freed through this field. The header's flag documentation (_IO_USER_LOCK) shows the slot is implementation-managed, and it can be null for a stream glibc has not finished initializing.

Head of the intrusive list of stream markers. A marker is created and destroyed by the code that registers it (the C++ streambuf protocol this layout preserves); closing the stream detaches the list without freeing its nodes, so the field borrows rather than owns. Null for every stream this tree opens.

Wide-character buffer state that glibc allocates together with the stream and tears down with it, so the slot must not be released on its own. Written throughout wide-oriented I/O; null when a stream carries no wide state.

types.name: addrinfo
types._comment_agent: Reviewed 2026-08-23 against /usr/include/netdb.h and crypto/bio/bio_addr.c. The releaser is selected by the PRODUCER, not by the node: a chain from getaddrinfo must be released with freeaddrinfo, and every chain returned by BIO_lookup/BIO_lookup_ex must be released with BIO_ADDRINFO_free. BIO_ADDRINFO_free itself dispatches on bai_family - it forwards resolver chains to freeaddrinfo and walks the AF_UNIX nodes it allocated itself - so one owner strategy covers both kinds of OpenSSL list, and the layout still binds no unconditional CDropped because nothing in a node identifies its producer. addrinfo_wrap leaves ai_addrlen and ai_canonname zero, so BIO_ADDRINFO_sockaddr_size reports 0 for those nodes.

ptr.note: Optional socket address of ai_addrlen bytes owned by the node. freeaddrinfo releases it with a resolver chain; a node built by addrinfo_wrap instead holds a BIO_ADDR from BIO_ADDR_new that BIO_ADDRINFO_free releases with OPENSSL_free, which is why the two origins cannot share one releaser. Consumers only read it: BIO_ADDRINFO_address and BIO_ADDRINFO_sockaddr both return it as const.

Optional NUL-terminated canonical name owned by a resolver-produced node and released by freeaddrinfo together with its chain. OpenSSL never populates it: addrinfo_wrap zero-allocates its nodes, and BIO_ADDRINFO_free's manual path releases only bai_addr and the node itself, so a hand-built node that set this field would leak it.

Owned tail of the node's chain. The head's releaser consumes every linked node: freeaddrinfo for a resolver chain, the manual OPENSSL_free loop in BIO_ADDRINFO_free for the AF_UNIX nodes addrinfo_wrap allocates. No consumer detaches, stores or frees a tail on its own, and BIO_ADDRINFO_next hands it back as const, so projected access must borrow the tail from the head.

types.name: asn1_object_st
types._comment_agent: ASN1_OBJECT conditionally owns its names and encoded bytes according to ASN1_OBJECT_FLAG_DYNAMIC_STRINGS/DATA. Built-in objects borrow immutable static tables, while transient non-dynamic objects may borrow caller storage; all three pointers are nullable.

ptr.note: A length-byte immutable OID buffer. DYNAMIC_DATA selects owned storage; built-in objects borrow static table bytes. The source states data remains const after initialization.
Owned and freed when DYNAMIC_STRINGS is set; otherwise built-in objects borrow immutable process-lifetime names. Transient stack objects may also borrow caller strings only for the enclosing call.
Owned and freed when DYNAMIC_STRINGS is set; otherwise built-in objects borrow immutable process-lifetime names. Transient stack objects may also borrow caller strings only for the enclosing call.

types.name: asn1_string_st
types._comment_agent: The data field has runtime-conditional ownership, selected by ASN1_STRING_FLAG_DATA_NOT_OWNED or ASN1_STRING_FLAG_NDEF; length is authoritative and the contents are not generally NUL-terminated. The header's own storage is equally conditional: ASN1_STRING_FLAG_EMBED, set by asn1_primitive_new for ASN1_EMBED template fields, means the struct lives inside a parent allocation and both destructors then release only the data. ASN1_STRING_free and ASN1_STRING_clear_free are ossl_asn1_string_free_internal with clear=0 and clear=1, so either accepts every string the other does and the choice between them is free.

ptr.note: Length-delimited byte buffer, normally owned and released by the ASN1_STRING destructor. Two flags suppress that release and make it a borrowed external buffer: ASN1_STRING_FLAG_DATA_NOT_OWNED, set by ASN1_STRING_new_not_owned, and ASN1_STRING_FLAG_NDEF, set by the streaming PKCS#7 and CMS code for a placeholder pointing into a caller buffer. ASN1_STRING_copy, and therefore ASN1_STRING_dup, allocates a fresh owned buffer and then copies every source flag except EMBED, so a copy of either kind of source owns its buffer while flagged as not owning it and leaks it at free (confirmed under LeakSanitizer). Zero-length strings may carry NULL. Mutating APIs can replace or write the buffer.

types.name: asn1_string_table_st
types._comment_agent: Reviewed 2026-08-23 against crypto/asn1/a_strnid.c, crypto/asn1/tbl_standard.h and include/openssl/asn1.h. A plain scalar record with two storage classes discriminated by the flags field. STABLE_FLAGS_MALLOC marks an entry that stable_get allocated with OPENSSL_zalloc and pushed onto the process-global `stable` stack; ASN1_STRING_TABLE_cleanup releases exactly those through st_free. An entry without the bit is an element of the static const tbl_standard array compiled into the library. ASN1_STRING_TABLE_get casts that constness away and may return either kind, so the result is borrowed, is invalidated by cleanup, and may only be written when it carries STABLE_FLAGS_MALLOC - which is the check stable_get makes before handing a record to ASN1_STRING_TABLE_add for update. STABLE_NO_MASK on the same field tells ASN1_STRING_set_by_NID to use mask directly instead of intersecting it with the global default mask. There is no public per-record destructor.

types.name: asn1_type_st
types._comment_agent: The value union is discriminator-controlled. Heap ASN1_TYPE values created by OpenSSL own active pointer payloads; ASN1_TYPE_free dispatches their release. The common ptr view also appears in non-owning stack temporaries. Pointer arms are nullable; string-shaped payloads are mutable internally, while ASN1_OBJECT payloads are observed immutably. Reviewed 2026-08-23: the ASN1_VALUE spelling of value.asn1_value names the union's generic aliasing slot, not the pointee, so V_ASN1_OTHER and every unenumerated tag carry an ASN1_STRING and only V_ASN1_ANY carries a nested ASN1_TYPE.

ptr.note: When this union arm is active, a fully constructed ASN1_TYPE owns the pointee and releases it according to the type discriminator; null is permitted.

The union's generic aliasing slot, not a distinct ASN1_VALUE payload: asn1_ex_c2i (tasn_dec.c), asn1_ex_i2c (tasn_enc.c), ossl_asn1_primitive_free (tasn_fre.c) and asn1_print_fsname (tasn_prn.c) all take &typ->value.asn1_value whatever the discriminator is. A fully constructed ASN1_TYPE owns the payload and the discriminator picks the releaser: ASN1_OBJECT_free for V_ASN1_OBJECT; a recursive ossl_asn1_primitive_free plus OPENSSL_free of the nested ASN1_TYPE for V_ASN1_ANY; ASN1_STRING teardown for every other tag, including V_ASN1_OTHER and every tag with no dedicated union member, which asn1_ex_c2i allocates as ASN1_STRING_type_new(tag). types.name: hostent
types._comment_agent: hostent has no independent lifecycle primitive: nothing in the tree allocates, frees or duplicates an entry or any buffer it points at, so it gets borrowed handles and no owning pointer form. The pointer fields are recorded borrowed with lifetime `self` rather than `static` deliberately. gethostbyname's storage is statically allocated but NOT valid for the life of the program -- the next lookup on the same thread overwrites it in place -- so the name, alias and address buffers are exactly as valid as the entry handle that reached them, and binding them to 'static would be wrong. The other producer, crypto/bio/bio_addr.c's `static const struct hostent he_fallback`, points h_addr_list at file-scope statics and is itself const, i.e. read-only storage; between the two, no producer in this tree yields a writable entry, so an exclusive handle is only ever legitimate over caller-owned storage. BIO_lookup_ex is the only in-tree field reader: it takes h_addrtype, h_length and h_addr_list, and walks the address vector without a NULL check on the vector itself. h_name and h_aliases are never read in-tree; their records describe the public struct hostent surface rather than observed OpenSSL behaviour.

BIO_lookup_ex reads the vector and every element but writes through neither, and dereferences the vector pointer without a NULL check -- nullable stays true because the public struct permits NULL, so a Rust getter should hand back an Option rather than inherit that assumption.

types.name: in6_addr
types._comment_agent: in6_addr is a by-value 16-byte address with no pointer fields, no refcount and no lifecycle primitive. Its three C union members alias the same 16 bytes: s6_addr keeps the network-order octets, while s6_addr16 and s6_addr32 reinterpret those bytes in host order, so the word views are byte-swapped against the wire on a little-endian target. Like in_addr it is read through BIO_ADDR_rawmake's untyped `const void *where` (`*(struct in6_addr *)where`, crypto/bio/bio_addr.c:158), so a wrapper must not assume the union's 4-byte alignment: the byte view is alignment-free, but the 16- and 32-bit views need unaligned loads and stores.

types.name: in_addr
types._comment_agent: in_addr is a by-value 4-byte IPv4 address. Its single s_addr field is network-order scalar data; there is no pointer field, no refcount and no lifecycle primitive, so it needs no owner and no releaser. It is NOT always reached through a properly aligned pointer: BIO_ADDR_rawmake takes an untyped `const void *where` and executes `*(struct in_addr *)where` at crypto/bio/bio_addr.c:148, and on the BIO_lookup_ex gethostbyname fallback path that argument is a hostent::h_addr_list element whose alignment the resolver does not promise. enable-ubsan reports exactly that misaligned load on the unmodified C tree (the disabled 90-test_quic_memfail.t baseline in crustify/build.json), so a Rust accessor over this type must use an unaligned load/store rather than assume the struct's 4-byte alignment.

types.name: obj_name_st
types._comment_agent: OBJ_NAME records own only their header allocation inside o_names.c: OBJ_NAME_add OPENSSL_mallocs one, and OBJ_NAME_add (on replacement), OBJ_NAME_remove and OBJ_NAME_cleanup OPENSSL_free it after running the class's registered free_func on the name/data pair. There is no public per-record constructor, destructor or clone. `alias` discriminates `data`: a non-zero alias makes data the borrowed name of another entry of the same class (OBJ_NAME_get feeds it back as its next lookup key), and a zero alias makes it the class's registered payload, an erased pointer that is NOT a string -- EVP_add_cipher and EVP_add_digest store (const char *)cipher / (const char *)md, and do_all_cipher_fn/do_all_md_fn cast it straight back. `type` and `name` are the hash key.

Either arm is stored without copying and OBJ_NAME_add does not validate it; NULL is reachable and reported by OBJ_NAME_get as `not registered`. Any external storage is governed by the class's optional free_func, never by OBJ_NAME itself.

OBJ_NAME_add stores the caller's const NUL-terminated name without copying it; registered callbacks receive that borrowed pointer. Every reader dereferences it unconditionally -- obj_name_cmp hands it to OPENSSL_strcasecmp, which derefs without a NULL check, and apps/enc.c:860 indexes it -- so a non-NULL name is the invariant the registry relies on. Transient optional source-file string. CRYPTO_clear_free never reads the (file, line) pair itself; it forwards it to CRYPTO_free, which forwards it verbatim to an application-installed CRYPTO_free_fn and otherwise calls free(str) alone (crypto/mem.c). NULL is inside that contract for the same reason it is for CRYPTO_free. In-tree C callers arrive through the OPENSSL_clear_free macro, which expands OPENSSL_FILE and OPENSSL_LINE (include/openssl/crypto.h).

Consumes a nullable allocation obtained from the active OpenSSL allocator; applies to scalar storage, counted buffers, and strings. NULL returns before anything else, so a null pointer is safe whatever num says. num is caller-asserted and never derived from the allocation: it is only the OPENSSL_cleanse length (crypto/mem_clr.c, an unelidable memset), so it must not exceed the live bytes, and it fixes how much is erased - bytes of the allocation beyond num survive the call. num == 0 skips the cleanse entirely (if (num) in crypto/mem.c), leaving the call identical to CRYPTO_free. Release then always goes through CRYPTO_free, so cleansing changes what the storage holds, never which allocator or application-installed CRYPTO_free_fn reclaims it: a buffer is interchangeable between CRYPTO_free and CRYPTO_clear_free owners.

CRYPTO_secure_clear_free never reads the (file, line) pair itself, and the arena branch discards it entirely; it reaches CRYPTO_free only on the ordinary-allocation branch, which forwards it verbatim to an application-installed CRYPTO_free_fn and otherwise calls free(ptr) alone (crypto/mem.c). Consumes a nullable allocation obtained from CRYPTO_secure_malloc / CRYPTO_secure_zalloc, whichever allocator actually served it; applies to scalar storage, counted buffers, and strings. NULL returns before anything else, so a null pointer is safe whatever num says. Like CRYPTO_secure_free it dispatches on the pointer's address through CRYPTO_secure_allocated -> sh_allocated (WITHIN_ARENA), and the two routines differ ONLY on the ordinary-allocation branch. Arena branch: num is IGNORED and the cleanse length is sh_actual_size(ptr), the whole buddy block (the request rounded up), so the erasure is at least what the caller asked for and the call is indistinguishable from CRYPTO_secure_free. Ordinary branch: num is exactly the OPENSSL_cleanse length (crypto/mem_clr.c, an unelidable memset) - caller-asserted, never derived from the allocation, so it must not exceed the live bytes, and bytes past it survive into free(). Unlike CRYPTO_clear_free there is no `if (num)` guard around the cleanse, but OPENSSL_cleanse(ptr, 0) is a no-op memset, so num == 0 leaves the call equivalent to CRYPTO_secure_free. Release then goes through CRYPTO_free on that branch, the same allocator CRYPTO_secure_free uses there, so cleansing changes what the storage holds and never which allocator reclaims it: a buffer is interchangeable between CRYPTO_secure_free and CRYPTO_secure_clear_free owners. Under OPENSSL_NO_SECURE_MEMORY only the ordinary branch remains. Release is not guaranteed to happen: on the arena branch a failing CRYPTO_THREAD_write_lock(sec_malloc_lock) returns without freeing, leaking the block. In-tree callers supply the full live extent - OPENSSL_secure_clear_free(a->data, a->max) in crypto/buffer/buffer.c, (a->d, a->dmax * sizeof(a->d[0])) in crypto/bn/bn_lib.c.

Consumes a nullable allocation obtained from CRYPTO_secure_malloc / CRYPTO_secure_zalloc, whichever allocator actually served it; applies to scalar storage, counted buffers, and strings. NULL returns before anything else. The branch is chosen from the pointer itself, not from anything the caller asserts: CRYPTO_secure_allocated -> sh_allocated is an arena address-range test (WITHIN_ARENA in crypto/mem_sec.c). Arena storage is cleansed over sh_actual_size(ptr) - the whole buddy block, i.e. the request rounded up to a power of two - and returned to the secure heap. Anything else is released through CRYPTO_free with its bytes INTACT: this routine never cleanses ordinary storage, and that is the path every allocation takes while the secure heap is down, because CRYPTO_secure_malloc/zalloc fall through to CRYPTO_malloc/CRYPTO_zalloc before CRYPTO_secure_malloc_init succeeds and after CRYPTO_secure_malloc_done. Under OPENSSL_NO_SECURE_MEMORY the entire body is that fallback. Consequences for pairing: this is a strict superset of CRYPTO_free - an ordinary OpenSSL allocation is released correctly here, only uncleansed - while the reverse is invalid, since CRYPTO_free would hand an arena address to free() or to an installed CRYPTO_free_fn. A buffer that may be secure must therefore be released by CRYPTO_secure_free or CRYPTO_secure_clear_free. Release is also not guaranteed to happen: on the arena branch a failing CRYPTO_THREAD_write_lock(sec_malloc_lock) returns without freeing, leaking the block.

The type's only release primitive: for a heap context it runs ossl_provider_deinit_child (child contexts), context_deinit and OPENSSL_free, and no other path frees an OSSL_LIB_CTX. It is total rather than exclusively owning: it returns early for NULL and for ossl_lib_ctx_is_default_nocreate(ctx), which matches BOTH the static default_context_int AND any context the calling thread installed as its default through OSSL_LIB_CTX_set0_default. The second case is the corner: that context is an ordinary heap context the caller owns, so the retained path is not limited to the process-global default, and freeing a current default leaks the context instead of corrupting it. The type has no reference count and no up_ref or dup, so this is the whole lifecycle. Rust owners only adopt constructor results and never the default, which keeps the owning path exact.

Declared void * but used as void **: every call site passes &ctx->ex_arg and every implementation dereferences it (ndef_prefix does ndef_aux = *(NDEF_SUPPORT **)parg). The outer slot is a borrowed cell; implementations guard it with an explicit parg == NULL check, hence nullable. The inner context pointer has dual ownership: the setup role and ndef_prefix_free only borrow it, while ndef_suffix_free consumes it (OPENSSL_free(*pndef_aux)) and writes NULL back, so the cleanup role is where the context is released. The prefix/suffix buffer of arg1 hangs off this context, which is why the two slots must be handed to the same setup/cleanup family.

Consumes a nullable byte buffer owned by the caller. Declared static ossl_inline in an internal header, so there is no linkable symbol to call: a Rust surface is a native translation of the branch it selects, not an FFI wrap. Both branches release through CRYPTO_free - OPENSSL_clear_free(ptr, size) -> CRYPTO_clear_free -> CRYPTO_free when OPENSSL_PEDANTIC_ZEROIZATION is defined, OPENSSL_free(ptr) -> CRYPTO_free otherwise - so the storage is an ordinary OpenSSL allocation whichever way the module is configured and only the cleansing differs; a buffer therefore crosses between C and a Rust owner in either build. size is read only on the pedantic branch, where it becomes the OPENSSL_cleanse length and must be the buffer's live byte count; the default branch ignores it, so a wrong size is inert there and harmful only under pedantic zeroization. Every in-tree caller is crypto/ffc/ffc_params.c (ossl_ffc_params_cleanup, ossl_ffc_params_set_seed, ossl_ffc_params_copy), passing params->seed with params->seedlen: an OPENSSL_memdup buffer of exactly seedlen bytes, or the NULL/0 pair ossl_ffc_params_init leaves behind. OPENSSL_PEDANTIC_ZEROIZATION is a supported configuration exercised daily in CI (.github/workflows/run-checker-daily.yml), not dead code.
